_comment: Field requirements the downstream filing module must collect, per Online Financial Fraud sub-category. Mandatory/common set mirrors what the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (cybercrime.gov.in) actually requires for a financial-fraud report. Per RBL Bank's portal guide (report-cybercrime-india-national-portal) and the portal's own intake: only incident date/time, a 200+ char description, complainant ID proof, the bank/wallet/merchant name, the 12-digit transaction ID/UTR, the transaction date, and the fraud amount are mandatory. ALL suspect/fraudster details are optional. Set verifiedAgainstPortalOn once re-checked directly on the live form.

mandatory_fields.label: Date and time the fraud happened
A description of what happened, in your own words (at least 200 characters)
A photo/scan of your ID (Aadhaar, PAN, Voter ID, Driving Licence, or Passport) — JPG/PNG, up to 5 MB
Name of the bank, wallet, or merchant involved

optional_fields.label: Screenshots, statements, or other proof (up to 10 MB each)
Suspect's mobile number
Suspect's email ID
Suspect's bank account number
Suspect's address
Photo of the suspect — JPG/PNG, up to 5 MB
Suspicious website URL or social-media handle involved
Your mobile number
Your email address
State/UT where the incident occurred
District where the incident occurred
Have you already reported this to your bank? (yes/no)
Did you call the 1930 helpline? (yes/no)

upi_fraud.label: UPI fraud
upi_fraud.institution_field_hint: The bank whose account was debited (the UPI app is only a channel).
upi_fraud._flow_note: mandatory_fields below reflect exactly what the fileComplaint chat agent collects and hard-blocks filing on for UPI (lib/agents/fileComplaint.ts). The `common` block is the portal's full intake superset; the agent collects a subset and derives the rest (e.g. transaction_date from time-since-fraud, incident_description from the narrative).

mandatory_fields.label: Recipient's UPI ID / VPA (or the recipient's name / phone number)
When the fraud happened (time since the transaction)
Your PIN code or city (for jurisdiction routing)
What happened, in your own words (one or two sentences)

optional_fields.label: UPI app used (GPay, PhonePe, Paytm, BHIM, bank app)
Bank the money was debited from
Bank the money was credited to
Mobile number registered with the debited bank account
Bank debit SMS/alert text
Screenshots from the UPI app showing the transaction

upi_fraud.evidence_notes: Most useful: the bank SMS or statement line showing the debit, plus the UPI app transaction history screenshot showing the 12-digit UTR/RRN and the payee VPA.

card_fraud.label: Debit/credit card fraud
card_fraud.institution_field_hint: The bank that issued the card.

optional_fields.label: Card type (debit or credit)
Last 4 digits of the card
Merchant name / statement descriptor for the charge
Was the charge domestic or international?
Did you share an OTP/CVV/PIN? (yes/no)
Reference number for blocking the card
Screenshot/PDF of the card statement line

card_fraud.evidence_notes: Most useful: the card statement line for the disputed charge, the transaction SMS, and any dispute/chargeback reference already raised with the bank.

internet_banking_fraud.label: Internet banking fraud
internet_banking_fraud.institution_field_hint: Your bank (the account the money left).

optional_fields.label: Your account number (the one debited)
Transfer channel (NEFT / IMPS / RTGS / internal)
Beneficiary account number the money went to
Beneficiary bank IFSC
How your credentials were compromised (phishing link / fake call / malware)
The phishing email/SMS/website, if that was the vector
Screenshots of the transaction/confirmation

internet_banking_fraud.evidence_notes: Most useful: the net-banking transaction confirmation and the account statement showing the debit. If a phishing link or fake call led to it, include that message or the number.

vishing.label: Voice phishing (vishing)
vishing.institution_field_hint: The bank or wallet the money was ultimately taken from.

optional_fields.label: Phone number the fraudster called from
How the money then left (UPI / card / net banking / wallet)
Who the caller claimed to be (bank / KYC / police / delivery / etc.)
What you disclosed (OTP / CVV / PIN / screen-share / app install)
Any app they made you install (AnyDesk, TeamViewer, etc.)
Recording of the call, if you have one
Screenshot of your call log showing the number and time

vishing.evidence_notes: Most useful: a call-log screenshot showing the fraudster's number and timestamp, any recording, and the debit evidence for whichever payment method was used (UPI UTR, card statement line, net-banking confirmation, or wallet history).

ewallet_theft.label: E-wallet theft
ewallet_theft.institution_field_hint: The wallet provider (Paytm, PhonePe, Amazon Pay, Mobikwik, etc.).

optional_fields.label: Mobile number registered with the wallet
Where the money went (wallet handle / UPI ID / account)
How access was gained (OTP shared / SIM swap / phishing / device lost)
Fraudster's phone number
Wallet transaction history export/screenshot
Complaint/ticket reference raised with the wallet provider
Evidence of SIM swap (carrier SMS, no-network period), if applicable

ewallet_theft.evidence_notes: Most useful: the wallet's in-app transaction history for the unauthorised debit, the provider's dispute/ticket reference, and any SIM-swap evidence if your number was ported without consent.

demat_fraud.label: Demat/trading account fraud

optional_fields.label: Demat or trading account ID (client ID)
DP ID / BO ID
What happened (unauthorised trades / holdings transferred out / funds withdrawn)
Securities affected or amount withdrawn (INR)
How access was gained (credentials phished / OTP shared / email compromised)
Bank account any withdrawn funds landed in
Broker contract notes / trade ledger for the disputed activity
Account login and activity logs

demat_fraud.evidence_notes: Most useful: the broker's contract notes / trade ledger for the disputed activity, the account login and activity logs, the CDSL/NSDL transaction statement, and — if funds were withdrawn — the bank credit trail showing where they went.

email_takeover.label: Email account takeover leading to financial loss
email_takeover.institution_field_hint: The bank/card/wallet/investment account the loss actually occurred on.

optional_fields.label: Email address that was taken over
Email provider (Gmail, Outlook, Yahoo, company mail, etc.)
Were the recovery email/phone changed by the attacker? (yes/no)
Unfamiliar login location/device shown in account security
How the account was likely compromised (phishing / reused password / malware)
Email provider's login/activity history (Google 'Recent security activity', Microsoft sign-in logs)
Password-reset or 'new sign-in' emails you received

email_takeover.evidence_notes: Most useful: the email provider's login/activity history, the attacker's password-reset or sign-in-alert emails, and the downstream bank/card/wallet debit evidence for the resulting loss.
